---
title: "System Network"
subtitle: "Connectivity between chromatographic systems"
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(rePredRet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# Statistics are computed from the published model index, so they are always current
index <- tryCatch(rePredRet_models(), error = function(e) NULL)
has_data <- !is.null(index) && nrow(index) > 0

systems <- tryCatch(rePredRet_systems(), error = function(e) NULL)
```

## Network Overview

The network shows how chromatographic systems are connected through pairwise models. Each node is a system and each edge a model between two systems (models are directional: one per source/target pair). Models are only built between systems of the same method type (reversed-phase with reversed-phase, HILIC with HILIC), since the elution order differs between the types.

```{r network-summary}
#| echo: false
if (has_data) {
  n_nodes <- length(unique(c(index$sys1_id, index$sys2_id)))
  n_edges <- nrow(index)
  type <- if (!is.null(systems)) systems$method.type[match(index$sys1_id, systems$id)] else NA
  models_by_type <- table(type)

  summary_table <- data.frame(
    Metric = c(
      "Total Systems (Nodes)",
      "Total Models (Edges)",
      paste0("Models between ", names(models_by_type), " systems"),
      "Average Models per System (as source)",
      "Network Density"
    ),
    Value = c(
      n_nodes,
      format(n_edges, big.mark = ","),
      format(as.integer(models_by_type), big.mark = ","),
      round(n_edges / n_nodes, 1),
      sprintf("%.2f%%", n_edges / (n_nodes * (n_nodes - 1)) * 100)
    )
  )
  kable(summary_table, align = "lr")
} else {
  cat("The model index could not be loaded.")
}
```

## Network Visualization

Each point is a system, sized by its number of compounds; the shape shows the
method type. Hover over a system to see its name.

How close two systems are is measured by their similarity: the Jaccard index
of their compounds, i.e. shared compounds divided by the compounds in either
system. Unlike the number of shared compounds, it does not make every system
look close to the few very large ones. The systems are placed using only the
links with a similarity of at least 0.4, so that systems sharing most of their
compounds end up together. All pairs sharing at least 20 compounds are then
drawn, wider and darker the more similar they are, so weak links fade into the
background. The slider hides the links below a chosen similarity.

The colours are groups of systems that share many compounds, found from all
pairs. Dark bundles between groups are many pairs of systems in two groups
that share a fair part of their compounds.

```{r network-plot}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "100%"
if (has_data) {
  plotly::layout(rePredRet_plot_network(min_compounds = 20, interactive = TRUE), height = 800)
}
```

## Connectivity Statistics

### Systems with Most Connections

```{r most-connected}
#| echo: false
if (has_data) {
  outgoing <- count(index, system_id = sys1_id, name = "n_outgoing")
  incoming <- count(index, system_id = sys2_id, name = "n_incoming")

  connections <- full_join(outgoing, incoming, by = "system_id") %>%
    mutate(
      n_outgoing = coalesce(n_outgoing, 0L),
      n_incoming = coalesce(n_incoming, 0L),
      total = n_outgoing + n_incoming
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(total)) %>%
    head(20)

  if (!is.null(systems)) {
    connections$name <- systems$name[match(connections$system_id, systems$id)]
    connections <- connections[, c("system_id", "name", "n_outgoing", "n_incoming", "total")]
    col_names <- c("System", "Name", "Outgoing", "Incoming", "Total")
  } else {
    col_names <- c("System", "Outgoing", "Incoming", "Total")
  }

  kable(connections, col.names = col_names, caption = "Top 20 most connected systems")
}
```

### Connection Distribution

```{r connection-histogram}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
#| echo: false
if (has_data) {
  all_connections <- bind_rows(
    count(index, system_id = sys1_id),
    count(index, system_id = sys2_id)
  ) %>%
    group_by(system_id) %>%
    summarize(total_connections = sum(n), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot(all_connections, aes(x = total_connections)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = median(all_connections$total_connections),
               color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(
      x = "Number of Connections (models as source or target)",
      y = "Number of Systems",
      title = "Distribution of System Connectivity"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14)
}
```

## Models by Compound Count

```{r models-by-compounds}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
#| echo: false
if (has_data) {
  ggplot(index, aes(x = n_compounds)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    labs(
      x = "Number of Common Compounds (log scale)",
      y = "Number of Models",
      title = "Distribution of Model Sizes"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14)
}
```

## Similarity Matrix

All pairs of systems, ordered by group (the colours of the network) and within
each group by similarity. Dark blocks on the diagonal are groups of systems that
share most of their compounds; off-diagonal blocks show how much the groups
overlap.

```{r similarity-matrix}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 11
#| echo: false
if (has_data) {
  rePredRet_plot_system_matrix(min_compounds = 20)
}
```
